3.title: Live order history on buyers
3.desc: Spend, outstanding balance, and product lines sync from Orders onto each buyer detail view so penetration gaps are visible per shop.

1.title: Next-best product to retailer matching

products.title: Catalog control for the full portfolio
products.subtitle: Maintain variants, pricing, MOQ, and stock so underused SKUs stay visible, available, and ready to introduce to suitable retailers.

overview.summary: Products is your wholesale catalog control room. Draft until variants, pricing, stock, and images are ready, then publish to your private Marketplace. A clear catalog is the base for spotting which SKUs under-penetrate eligible retailers.

1.title: Publish to your private Marketplace
1.desc: Complete the catalog once in Dashboard. Publish with readiness checks so authorised retailers see the same SKUs, images, and stock.

2.title: Wholesale variants with MOQ and stock
2.desc: Each size or flavor combination carries its own SKU, selling price, minimum order quantity, and piece-level stock buyers must meet at checkout.

3.title: A rate for each retailer
3.desc: Attach an offer rate to a retailer. Marketplace cards keep the catalog base price.

1.title: Assortment gap detection with heatmap
1.desc: Visualise which products under-penetrate eligible retailers on a heatmap so low assortment coverage stands out before you plan introductions.

2.desc: Incomplete products stay in draft. Publish only when name, variants, pricing, stock greater than zero, and images pass Marketplace readiness gates.

3.desc: Set selling price, purchase price, MOQ, and low-stock thresholds on every variation combination, not a single flat SKU.

offers.title: Per-retailer terms that unlock introductions
offers.subtitle: Set a percentage, fixed amount, or Buy X Get Y rate for a specific retailer so underused products can be introduced on commercial terms that fit that shop.

overview.summary: Offers are per retailer, not a public price change. Assign a rate to a buyer and a product or category when you activate a portfolio opportunity. Marketplace cards keep the catalog base price. When that retailer orders, their rate is the one on the purchase order.

1.title: One shop, one rate
1.desc: The same SKU can carry a different rate for each retailer. Other shops still see the catalog base price.

2.title: The shelf stays the base price
2.desc: Activating an offer does not rewrite Marketplace cards. The rate waits for that retailer's purchase order.

3.title: A window you control
3.desc: Set a start and end so the rate is active only while you want that retailer to order on those terms.

1.title: Product offer rates per retailer
1.desc: Set and manage product-level rates for each retailer in one list, so every shop keeps commercial terms that fit how you introduce and sell to them.

2.title: Three ways to set the rate
2.desc: Use a percentage, a fixed amount, or Buy X Get Y, tied to that retailer and the products they buy.

3.title: Catalog price stays the reference
3.desc: Retailers browse the base price. Their own rate does not change what other shops see.

4.title: The rate lands on the purchase order
4.desc: When that retailer orders, the purchase order uses their rate. You send the price when you want it confirmed.

5.title: See which rates were used
5.desc: Track usage and discount given on each offer so you know which retailer rates actually moved volume.

sales.title: Sales work that uses limited time well

moat.title: Built for the portfolio problem enterprise tools miss
moat.subtitle: Independent Indonesian FMCG distributors do not lack products. They lack a systematic way to see which products under-penetrate eligible retailers, which shops are suitable, and how to use scarce sales time. Lakupak is built for that.

1.title: Assortment penetration, not vanity reach
1.desc: Bestsellers dominate repeat orders while other potentially valuable SKUs stay stuck with a small share of eligible retailers, often without anyone knowing where extra demand might exist.

2.title: Product–retailer matching
2.desc: Sales teams cannot evaluate every product against every retailer by hand. Familiar bestsellers keep getting pitched while suitable combinations go unexplored.

3.title: Connected commercial data
3.desc: Catalogs, relationships, purchase history, offers, and sales activity are usually fragmented. Patterns that would surface real opportunities stay invisible.

4.title: Scarce sales attention
4.desc: Reps have limited time per retailer. Interactions stay brief, relevant products go unpresented, and portfolio potential stays locked in the warehouse.

5.title: Investigate, do not push everything
5.desc: Low penetration is not automatic unmet demand. A product may be unsuitable, mispriced, out of stock, or unpopular. Lakupak helps distinguish credible opportunities from noise.

6.title: Private commerce under distributor control
6.desc: Authorised retailers order from your private storefront with your pricing and terms. Commercial intelligence creates value without surrendering relationships or data.

comparison.title: Plan comparison
comparison.subtitle: Every plan includes the full platform. Tiers differ by usage capacity.

1.a: Plans are based on active retail connections: buyers in your Clients module that have placed at least one order in the last 90 days. Your tier is applied from that count on each billing date.

2.a: Yes. Every new distributor gets a 30-day free trial with full Dashboard access. Billing starts on day 31 if you continue.

3.q: What are the benefits of annual billing?
3.a: Annual billing is priced at 10× the monthly rate (2 months free), about 17% savings versus paying month to month.

4.q: What payment methods do you accept?
4.a: We accept bank transfer (BCA, Mandiri, BRI), virtual accounts, and credit/debit cards.

5.q: Can I upgrade or downgrade my plan?
5.a: Yes. As your active retail connections grow, you can move to a higher tier. Downgrades take effect at the next billing cycle.

6.q: Do all plans include Dashboard and Marketplace?
6.a: Yes. Every plan includes Dashboard and the Marketplace buyer app, with no feature gating by tier. Plans differ by usage capacity such as products, sales agents, and orders.

7.a: Enterprise is for distributors with 10,000+ active retailers who need custom pricing, SLA, and onboarding support. Contact sales for a quote.

8.q: What happens if I reach a usage limit?
8.a: We use soft caps during MVP: you get a warning around 80% of a quota and an upgrade nudge if you go over. We do not hard-block mid-cycle yet. Optional hard caps (for example new product publishes) may be added later.

hero.subtitle: To help independent FMCG distributors in Indonesia unlock underused products across the retailers they already serve.

story.1: For as long as I can remember, trade has been the lifeblood of local communities. In Indonesia, independent distributors, warungs, and neighbourhood shops keep daily essentials within reach. From the outside it looks busy. From the inside, many distributors manage hundreds of products across hundreds of retailers, yet a narrow set of bestsellers still dominates repeat orders.
story.2: The rest of the portfolio often stalls. A product may reach only a small share of eligible shops, with no clear view of where additional demand might exist. Sales teams cannot thoroughly evaluate every product against every retailer. They keep promoting what is familiar. Suitable product–retailer opportunities stay unexplored. Good products get missed, not always because retailers refuse them, but because nothing systematically matches the right product to the right shop.
story.3: Commercial data makes the problem harder to see. Catalogs live in one place, relationships in another, purchase history in chats and spreadsheets, offers and sales activity somewhere else. Patterns that would reveal assortment gaps stay fragmented. Meanwhile reps have limited time per visit. Interactions stay brief. Relevant products go unpresented. Potential sales remain locked in the portfolio.
story.4: The problem is not that every product must sell more. Some SKUs are unsuitable, mispriced, unavailable, or genuinely unpopular. What distributors lack is a systematic way to distinguish genuine growth opportunities from limited demand, identify suitable retailers, and make scarce sales interactions more productive.
story.5: That is when the real problem came into focus. This was not “digitise distribution” in the abstract. It was product portfolio underutilisation and low assortment penetration, the specific challenge facing Indonesian FMCG distribution, paired with fragmented data and inefficient field execution.
story.6: I built Lakupak to connect distributor operations, AI-powered sales intelligence, and private B2B commerce. Unify the commercial record. Identify penetration gaps and product–retailer combinations worth investigating. Prioritise with evidence. Activate sales teams with focused recommendations. Convert through a private marketplace where authorised retailers order under the distributor’s control. Learn from exposure, responses, and orders, without treating recommendations as guaranteed demand.
story.pausedMarketplace: Authorised retailers discover products through the distributor’s private storefront.
story.7: The name carries the same idea. In Indonesian, laku means both a sale and movement. Trade moves when the right products reach the right retailers, and when sales time is spent on opportunities supported by evidence. Lakupak exists to make that movement deliberate, not accidental.
story.8: A distributor should not have to push every SKU to every shop. They should know where the portfolio is underused, where it is constrained, and where to act next. That is what Lakupak is built to give back.
story.mission: We are only at the start. The mission is still clear: help independent FMCG distributors utilise their product portfolios across existing retailers, improve sales execution, and preserve trust over commercial data.
story.end: And this is just the start.

1.title: Our Mission
1.content: Help distributors connect the right products with the right retailers, make sales interactions more productive, and turn commercial data into actionable opportunities, without compromising control or trust.

2.title: Our Vision
2.content: An AI-native B2B commerce and sales platform for Indonesian FMCG distribution: portfolio intelligence, focused sales activation, and private commerce under distributor control.

3.1: Low penetration is a signal to investigate, not proof of demand.
3.2: Every retailer has their own terms, and those terms stay under the distributor’s control.
3.3: The right product–retailer match is what makes limited sales time pay off.
